newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares erase gains, end slightly off.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares erase gains, end slightly off.

text.p: Brazilian stocks gave back early gains and closed slightly off on Friday, mirroring the Dow Industrials which traded lower for most of the session, brokers said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most liquid shares fell 0.01 percent, closing at 9,302 points.
Market turnover was 564.1 million reais ($532.1 million).

Some brokers also attributed market weakness to concerns over the implications of a Senate inquiry looking into allegations of a multi-million dollar bond scam after Sao Paulo mayor Celso Pitta became the focus of the investigations.

The latest evidence senators produced against the mayor, then Sao Paulo city Finance Secretary, was a letter with his signature allegedly authorizing the sale of $70 million in municipal bonds to Banco Vetor, a medium-sized bank that made huge profits out of the bond scam.
Investors had been ignoring the congressional inquiry but now they fear the consequences of Pitta's alleged involvement in the scandal if it is proved to be true.
Analysts also said the market is likely to remain volatile ahead of next week's U.S. Federal Reserve meeting in which a decision on a rise in U.S. interest rates may be taken.
Benchmark Telebras preferred managed to end 0.44 percent higher at 113 reais, while its common stock rose 2.06 percent to 109.70 reais.
State mining giant Vale do Rio Doce fell 2.29 percent to 25.250 reais.
